caveats:
The product contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2021-2022), processed by ESA and analyzed by the Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS), using the Advanced Rapid Imaging and Analysis (ARIA) system originally developed at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology, and modified at EOS-RS.

The product contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2022), processed by ESA and analyzed by the Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS), using the Advanced Rapid Imaging and Analysis (ARIA) system originally developed at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology, and modified at EOS-RS.

This map was derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images acquired by the ALOS-2 satellites operated by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) before (21 May 2020 and 19 May 2022) and after (22 Sep 2022) the event.

These are preliminary maps derived from satellite radar and should be used as guidance only. Coloured pixels may include false positives, and their absence does not mean an absence of damage or flooding.
methodology_other: Change detection on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images acquired before and after the event. Damage Proxy Maps show significant changes in radar coherence and amplitude; Flood Proxy Maps show areas that changed to standing water. Maps are preliminary and checked against news reports and ground-level imagery where available.

# Taiwan Earthquake: Damage Proxy Maps, Sep 2022

The **Earth Observatory of Singapore – Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS)** produced these damage proxy maps for Taiwan Earthquake (Sep 2022) from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images. Each map is a separate ZIP below with its GeoTIFF, a KMZ for Google Earth, the PNG figures and a text file describing how it was made and how to read it.

## Maps in this dataset

- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Taiwan, Earthquake, 24 Sep 2022, v0.9**
- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Taiwan, Earthquake, 24 Sep 2022, v0.9**
- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Taiwan, Earthquake, 22 Sep 2022, v0.9**
- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Taiwan, Earthquake, 22 Sep 2022, v0.9**
- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Taiwan, Earthquake, 22 Sep 2022, v0.4** (superseded)
- **EOS-RS Damage Proxy Map: Taiwan, Earthquake, 22 Sep 2022, v0.4** (superseded)

**More map details and files:** <https://sf.earthobservatory.sg/event/EOS-RS_202209_Taiwan_Earthquake>

**More map details and files:** <http://eos-rs-products.earthobservatory.sg/EOS-RS_202209_Taiwan_Earthquake/>

organization.title: Earth Observatory of Singapore
organization.description: The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) is a research lab at Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore. It uses satellite remote sensing, mainly synthetic aperture radar (SAR), to map natural hazards and disasters. The lab produces Damage Proxy Maps (DPMs) and Flood Proxy Maps (FPMs) showing where damage or flooding has likely occurred. Its work focuses on Southeast Asia and the wider Asia-Pacific, and it also responds to major disasters worldwide.

This map was derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images acquired by the Copernicus Sentinel-1 satellites operated by the European Space Agency (ESA) before (16 Dec 2021 to 12 Sep 2022) and after (24 Sep 2022) the event.
